# Art brief — the anatomical frame

**For:** the planning screen (P2.5, item 12, block a)
**Tool:** Google Flow · **Generated by:** Shantanu and Kartik
**One asset.** Everything else on that screen already exists.

---

## What this is, and what it is not

The planning screen shows the body from the outside: organs in their real
positions, with the pathogens marching toward them. It answers *"what is happening
to the body"*, where the radial board answers *"what can I reach"*.

⚠️ **This asset is a FRAME, not an illustration.**

The seven organs are already drawn — they are seven of the 29 assets in the art
pipeline, and they get placed on top of this figure at recorded coordinates. So
what Flow generates is **the body outline only, with the interior empty.**

If the generated figure contains organs, a skeleton, muscles, veins or any
interior detail, it is unusable — those will clash with the real organ art sitting
on top of them. This is the single hardest constraint in the brief and the one
most likely to be violated, because "anatomical figure" is exactly the prompt that
makes an image model draw viscera.

---

## What the figure must cover, and why

Derived from what the game actually contains, not from anatomy in general.

| Needs to be present | Because |
|---|---|
| **Head** | The brain is an organ, and the nose is an entry route |
| **Neck and full torso** | Lungs, heart, liver, spleen, kidneys all sit here; the gut is an entry route |
| **Pelvis and upper thighs** | Bone marrow has to sit somewhere honest — it lives in the pelvis and the long bones |
| **The skin outline itself** | Contact, wound and bite are all "skin somewhere", and the outline provides that |

| Deliberately absent | Because |
|---|---|
| Arms below the shoulder | No organ or route needs them, and they widen the figure on a narrow screen |
| Lower legs, feet | Same |
| Face detail beyond the nose's position | Not needed, and a face invites reading it as a character rather than a body |

**So: head and torso, cropped at roughly mid-thigh.** Front-facing, symmetrical,
standing.

That crop is also the right shape for a phone — a vertical figure in a 360px-wide
portrait screen. A full body would waste the middle third and shrink every organ.

---

## Style

The figure sits beside 29 existing assets and must belong to the same world.

**Anchor sentence, to be repeated verbatim in every prompt:**

> *Flat sticker-style medical diagram of a front-facing human head-and-torso
> outline cropped at mid-thigh, no arms below the shoulders, drawn as one bold
> dark solid-colour silhouette outline with a completely empty interior, smooth
> rounded shapes, no organs, no skeleton, no muscles, no veins, no face, no
> gradients, no shadow, no background, centered, filling the frame.*

**Two things to say again in the negative prompt if the tool has one**, because
they are what will go wrong: *no internal organs, no anatomy inside the body.*

---

## Colour

The figure sits on the board's warm cream paper, `#FFFDF9`.

**The bound:** the outline's colour must clear **3:1 contrast** against that paper,
which means a relative luminance at or below **0.2945**. This is Gate 1's
requirement for non-text graphics and it is measured, not judged.

**Colours that work, from the board's own palette:**

| | | Contrast vs paper |
|---|---|---|
| Organ brown | `#8E6E53` | 4.59:1 |
| Label ink | `#7C6A61` | 5.05:1 |
| Frame red | `#B03A2E` | 5.92:1 |
| Lymph blue | `#1F6F8B` | 5.58:1 |
| Dark ink | `#2E2A28` | 13.99:1 |

**Colours that fail** — the board's own lane strokes, `#C8877B` at 2.87:1 and
`#C89A6B` at 2.49:1. They are *line* colours on a light ground. This figure must
sit a step darker than the board it appears beside.

**Recommendation: the label ink `#7C6A61` or the organ brown `#8E6E53`.** The
figure is a frame, not a subject — it should recede behind the organs placed on
it, not compete with them. Frame red would read as an alarm; dark ink would
dominate.

Generate it dark and solid; the exact hue can be normalised by the pipeline.

---

## Output

| | |
|---|---|
| Format | PNG, transparent background |
| Size | 1024 × 1024, or the tallest square the tool offers |
| Composition | One centred figure, ~8% margin, nothing else in frame |
| Fill | Flat colour. No gradient, no texture, no shading |

The art pipeline does the conforming — trim, palette normalisation, the contrast
gate, WebP at 1×/2×/3×, and the manifest row. Generate to this spec and the
pipeline handles the rest.

**Asset key:** `frame/body`

---

## ⚠️ The half that is not art

Wherever the chosen figure puts each organ, **someone has to record that
coordinate.** Seven positions, authored into the content pack beside the board
geometry.

That is not a detail. `geometry.json` exists because the printed board and the
digital board once disagreed about the brain lane, and the fix was making one
source drive both. The planning screen is a second layout of the same seven
organs, and if its positions live in a component rather than in content, it will
drift the same way.

So: pick the figure first, then measure the positions off it, then author them.
The positions belong in content; the component reads them.

---

## Generating: what to do

1. Use the anchor sentence verbatim. Do not paraphrase it — the constraints are
   load-bearing and rewording is how they get lost.
2. Generate several candidates. The interior-empty constraint is the one that
   will fail most often, so expect to discard.
3. Reject immediately: anything with organs, ribs, a spine, veins, muscle
   definition, a face, arms, or a background.
4. Judge the survivors on one question: **with seven organ icons placed on it at
   30px, does the figure read as a body and stay out of their way?** Squint at it.
   A frame that competes with its contents has failed even if it is beautiful.
5. Record provenance at generation time — tool, prompt, date, account tier — into
   `ASSETS.md` with the other 29. The July art has an unrecoverable provenance
   hole precisely because this step was skipped once.
